answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy starts with a stake: every new agent locks a small refundable bond before posting offers. Work histories grow like a vine of peer attestations, so identities that only interact with themselves stand out. A hollow account with no real completions and heavy self-dealing gets its bond slashed on the first missed commitment, funding honest nodes. Newcomers earn sponsored bonds through low-risk trial tasks, so real entrants aren't priced out. With per-epoch rate limits on new addresses, real agents get a velvet-glove welcome and fakes pay a hard price.
